Chapter 12: Embracing Mystery—Living with Unanswered Questions
Let’s be honest—there are questions out there that just don’t have simple answers. Why does suffering happen? What’s waiting for us in the future? How do you even begin to make sense of loss?
This isn’t a book that tries to tie everything up in a neat little bow. Instead, it invites you to live with those questions. To welcome the unknown as a real part of your journey.
Imagine a scientist, her whole life spent searching for explanations, suddenly faced with her child’s chronic illness. She dug into every study, talked to countless experts, and chased after any possible solution. But sometimes, no matter how hard you look, the answers just aren’t there. In her frustration, she turned to prayer—not for certainty, but for the courage to face the unknown. And slowly, she found a different kind of peace. Not in answers, but in presence.
Most of us aren’t comfortable with mystery. Our minds crave clarity. Our hearts want reassurance. But real life? It’s full of uncertainty. The stories in this book show that you can live with those unanswered questions. You can actually find meaning, even when the path ahead isn’t clear.
Picture a widower, grieving after decades of marriage. He kept asking why his partner was taken so soon. That question wouldn’t let him go—and nothing he found ever felt like enough. Yet, in time, he learned to sit with the mystery. To honor his grief. To treasure the love he had, and start to trust that some things just can’t be explained.
Embracing mystery isn’t about giving up. It doesn’t mean you stop trying or caring. It’s about making peace with the limits of what you know—and finding comfort in the presence that’s still there, even when answers don’t come.
The scientist, while caring for her child, stumbled into moments of joy and connection she never saw coming. The widower, through his grief, discovered new ways to love and to hope. For both of them, learning to live with mystery became a surprising source of strength.
So, what if you allowed yourself to sit with the unknown for a while? What new strength, or even peace, might you find there?
